To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a human capital enhancing HR system, when combined with a quality manufacturing approach, is associated with superior plant performance.
a human capital enhancement strategy was positively related to operational performance, but this main effect was moderated by manufacturing strategy.
the relationship between HRM and manufacturing performance is contingent upon manufacturing strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the conditions under which HRM practices are most likely to be associated with firm performance and the mechanisms through which HRM practices affect firm performance.
understanding the role that manufacturing strategy and HRM play in explaining plant performance.
how HR systems and practices influence manufacturing performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HR performance relationship is contingent upon the manufacturing strategy employed by the plant.
a human capital enhancing HR system is a necessary but not sufficient condition for superior operational performance.
a human capital enhancing HR system is a critical ingredient of a quality strategy, which in turn, leads to superior manufacturing performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HR system should be aligned with the manufacturing strategy.
the relationship between HR and performance is contingent upon the manufacturing strategy.
the relationship between human resources and manufacturing performance is moderated by manufacturing strategy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HRM is not a universal good for manufacturing firms, but instead the value of HR systems depends on a firm’s manufacturing strategy.
HRM is an important strategic resource that can be leveraged in the manufacturing sector.
HR systems and manufacturing strategies are interdependent.
